newsitem.title: UK: BAe joins Lockheed strike fighter bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: BAe joins Lockheed strike fighter bid - paper.

text.p: British Aerospace (BAe) has chosen to join with Lockheed Martin rather than Boeing in a bid for a $200 billion U.S. order for a Joint Strike Fighter (JSF), The Sunday Times reported.
"Under the Lockheed deal, BAe may get a 15 percent stake in the American group's JSF bid, including extensive manufacturing work," the newspaper said.
The paper said the order for 3,000 fighters would be the largest combat aircraft order in history.

However, BAe joint managing director John Weston told Reuters at the Paris air show at the weekend that British Aerospace would pick which JSF team it would join shortly, but no decision had been made yet.
The Sunday Times said BAe's decision means Lockheed, which is already in talks about a tie-up with the Airbus civil aircraft consortium, will be its long-term American partner, it said.
Britain wants the naval version of the JSF to replace the Royal Navy's Harrier jump-jets, the newspaper said.
